question: Will the bridge weaken sanctions, yes or no?

lines.text: China and North Korea have opened the New Yalu River Bridge, twelve years late.
Xinhua says the opening ceremony was held today.
It links Dandong in China with Sinuiju in North Korea, across the Yalu River.
The road bridge is four lanes wide and three kilometres long.
China finished it in 2014, at a cost of about 2.2 billion yuan.
Officially, North Korea lacked roads and customs posts on its side.
The old 1937 bridge carries over seventy percent of official trade, one way at a time.
China says the new crossing can handle up to twenty thousand vehicles a day.
About ninety eight percent of North Korea's trade last year was with China.
Trade rose almost twenty percent in the first half of this year, to 1.5 billion dollars.
About a month ago, North Korea opened a smaller road bridge to Russia.
UN nuclear sanctions still apply, and a Seoul analyst says the bridge could weaken them.
Will the bridge weaken sanctions, yes or no?
